# The Origin of the Northern Lights

Long ago, when the world was young, the Sky Goddess Aelara had seven daughters who loved to dance. Each evening, they would twirl and leap across the heavens, their joy creating gentle starlight.

One winter, a terrible coldness gripped the earth. The people below suffered, and their prayers rose like smoke to the heavens. The seven sisters heard their cries and wept with compassion.

"We must help them," said the eldest sister. "Let us dance with all our hearts, so fiercely that our warmth reaches the frozen world below."

That night, the sisters danced as never before. They spun so fast their gowns became rivers of color—emerald green, sapphire blue, violet purple, and rose pink. The ribbons in their hair streamed behind them, painting brilliant waves across the dark sky.

The people below gazed up in wonder, feeling warmth return to their hearts. Though the winter remained cold, they no longer despaired, for the dancing lights reminded them that beauty and hope exist even in darkness.

To this day, the seven sisters dance in the northern sky, their colorful gowns shimmering and flowing, bringing wonder to all who witness their celestial performance.
